purpose: Record and enforce the canonical Rust Delivery domain and append-only store while the TypeScript product seam remains scheduled for removal.

canonicalRustAuthority.interface: A small command/query module owns validation and persistence; callers do not manipulate stored records directly.

rules.statement: A DeliverySpec contains at least one acceptance criterion and at least one criterion is required.

tests.name: DeliverySpec requires delivery boundaries and a bounded rework limit

rules.statement: Every DeliveryTask names at least one acceptance criterion from the current DeliverySpec.

typescript.gap: The TypeScript validator implements the relationship check, but no public test supplies an empty or foreign acceptanceCriterionIds set.

rules.statement: Every blockedByTaskId resolves to another DeliveryTask in the same Delivery.

typescript.gap: The TypeScript validator rejects a missing dependency, but the existing task graph test only supplies a two-node cycle.

rules.statement: A DeliveryTask cannot depend on itself.

typescript.gap: The TypeScript validator rejects a self-reference, but no public TypeScript test isolates that case.

rules.statement: The DeliveryTask dependency graph is acyclic.

tests.name: Delivery rejects duplicate and cyclic delivery-significant tasks

rules.statement: Running or waiting StageRuns have no finish time; settled StageRuns have a finish time at or after their start time.

typescript.gap: The TypeScript parser implements all status/time branches, but the public tests only use valid StageRuns.

rules.statement: A reworking StageRun uses actor type codex and role remediator.

tests.name: Delivery accepts Delivery- or task-scoped Codex remediators within the approved limit

rules.statement: The number of reworking StageRuns does not exceed the current DeliverySpec maxReworkAttempts.

tests.name: Delivery accepts Delivery- or task-scoped Codex remediators within the approved limit

rules.statement: A canonical SessionBinding starts with distinct ProductSession and ExecutionJob identities; WorkerSession and CodexThread are added only when their owners report them.

tests.name: Codex StageRuns require a Codex session binding and current relationships

typescript.gap: The legacy TypeScript binding only knows dshSessionId and codexSessionId. It cannot express the canonical ProductSession, ExecutionJob, WorkerSession, and CodexThread lifecycle; the Rust test is the new source of truth until the old TypeScript backend is removed.

rules.statement: A SessionBinding belongs to the same Delivery, an existing Codex StageRun, and that StageRun’s exact optional DeliveryTask; its binding time cannot predate the StageRun.

tests.name: Codex StageRuns require a Codex session binding and current relationships

typescript.gap: The legacy TypeScript aggregate checks Delivery, StageRun, and Codex actor relationships, but its SessionBinding has no DeliveryTask, ProductSession, or ExecutionJob identity. The exact Rust relationship is canonical.

rules.statement: Delivery status needs-attention requires at least one open blocking AttentionItem.

tests.name: needs-attention requires a durable open blocking item

rules.statement: A passing DeliveryVerdict cannot coexist with open blocking Attention except the final delivery approval.

tests.name: passing and delivered states fail closed on stale or failed evidence

rules.statement: A delivered Delivery has no open blocking AttentionItem, including delivery approval.

typescript.gap: The TypeScript validator contains this delivered-only check, but the existing blocking test is rejected earlier by the passing-verdict rule.

rules.statement: ready-to-deliver and delivered statuses require a passing DeliveryVerdict.

tests.name: passing and delivered states fail closed on stale or failed evidence

rules.statement: ready-to-deliver and delivered statuses require every DeliveryTask to be completed.

typescript.gap: The TypeScript validator implements this state rule, but no public test supplies an incomplete task with a delivery-ready status.

rules.statement: Every EvidenceRef belongs to the current DeliverySpec identity and exact revision.

tests.name: Codex StageRuns require a Codex session binding and current relationships
invalidates prior acceptance and candidate identities after definition or writer changes

rules.statement: Every EvidenceRef points to an existing StageRun in the same Delivery.

tests.name: Codex StageRuns require a Codex session binding and current relationships

rules.statement: Every EvidenceRef points to an existing SessionBinding for the same Delivery and StageRun.

tests.name: Codex StageRuns require a Codex session binding and current relationships
resolves runtime and Git facts to exact spec, candidate, stage, and session identities

rules.statement: Evidence creation time is not earlier than its StageRun start or SessionBinding time.

tests.name: Codex StageRuns require a Codex session binding and current relationships

rules.statement: CriterionResult evidence and frozen verification facts belong to the exact current candidate.

tests.name: passing and delivered states fail closed on stale or failed evidence
rejects stale acceptance, stale candidate, and foreign result identities

rules.statement: A pass or fail CriterionResult cites at least one EvidenceRef; inconclusive and infra_error may remain evidence-free.

tests.name: fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

typescript.gap: The higher-level verdict test covers missing direct evidence, but no parser test submits an evidence-free pass or fail CriterionResult.

rules.statement: A DeliveryVerdict evaluates every current acceptance criterion exactly once and no foreign criterion.

tests.name: computes one deterministic passing verdict from current direct evidence

typescript.gap: The computation test proves complete output, but no TypeScript parser test removes, duplicates, or adds one verdict criterion.

rules.statement: DeliveryVerdict status is derived from required CriterionResults and unresolved findings with fail, infra_error, inconclusive, then pass precedence.

tests.name: passing and delivered states fail closed on stale or failed evidence
fails closed for each non-passing verification condition

rules.statement: Reusing requestId with the same request digest and operation replays the original snapshot; any conflicting reuse is rejected.

tests.name: DeliveryStore replays one request and rejects conflicting reuse or revision

rules.statement: A mutation applies only when expectedRevision equals the stored revision and the new snapshot advances exactly one revision.

tests.name: DeliveryStore replays one request and rejects conflicting reuse or revision

rules.statement: Durable records have contiguous sequences and each previousDigest equals the prior record digest, beginning at the manifest firstRecordDigest.

tests.name: DeliveryStore creates, reopens, and replays one exact snapshot chain

rules.statement: A changed manifest, record, snapshot, sequence, relationship, request identity, or digest is rejected as store corruption.

tests.name: DeliveryStore ignores pending files and rejects a changed durable record

rules.statement: Concurrent writers may publish only one record for the same next revision; the loser receives a revision conflict.

tests.name: competing DeliveryStore instances publish one revision

rules.statement: An unpublished pending record is ignored during recovery; only the atomically published record chain is authoritative.

tests.name: DeliveryStore ignores pending files and rejects a changed durable record

contractFindings.current: The TypeScript Delivery domain exposes numeric DELIVERY_SCHEMA_VERSION 3.
contractFindings.target: The accepted phase-one public schema exposes the string schemaVersion winwincode/v1.
contractFindings.action: Keep numeric v3 only in the one-time legacy fixture importer; Rust public projections and commands use the generated winwincode/v1 type.

contractFindings.current: The TypeScript transition seam, canonical Rust aggregate, and generated public schemas accept only dlv_ followed by 26 uppercase Crockford Base32 characters.
contractFindings.target: GitHub issue sources retain sourceRef while both language seams deterministically map the normalized source bytes to the same canonical dlv_ identity; source-less creation generates a ULID-shaped dlv_ identity.
contractFindings.action: Enforce the versioned GitHub source mapping, reject caller overrides and github-issue: identities, and keep sourceRef as the external issue binding.

contractFindings.current: The TypeScript Delivery entities expose non-negative integer millisecond timestamps.
contractFindings.target: The phase-one public schema exposes UTC date-time strings with exactly millisecond precision.
contractFindings.action: Choose one internal Rust instant representation and convert exactly once in the public projection adapter; do not expose two timestamp formats.

contractFindings.current: The legacy TypeScript SessionBinding still stores dshSessionId and codexSessionId, while the canonical Rust SessionBinding now keeps ProductSessionId, ExecutionJobId, WorkerSessionId, and CodexThreadId distinct.
contractFindings.target: ADR-0028 requires the Rust SessionBinding to be the only backend contract and removes DSH identities when the TypeScript backend is cut over.
contractFindings.action: Keep legacy fields only as one-time migration input, reject mixed old/new shapes, and delete the TypeScript backend binding after cutover; do not expose either legacy field through the new public schema.

contractFindings.current: The ten-object TypeScript model gives DeliverySpec, AcceptanceCriterion, SessionBinding, CriterionResult, and DeliveryVerdict their own IDs and calls the evidence identity EvidenceRefId.
contractFindings.target: The phase-one public schema defines EvidenceId but does not define public IDs for those five internal Delivery objects.
contractFindings.action: Define the five missing identities inside the Rust Delivery domain and use generated EvidenceId; any future wire exposure requires a separate canonical-schema decision.

contractFindings.current: TypeScript validators and store expose detailed codes such as RELATIONSHIP_MISMATCH, INVALID_VERDICT, REQUEST_CONFLICT, and STORE_CORRUPT.
contractFindings.target: The phase-one wire contract exposes stable public codes including INVALID_REQUEST, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, REVISION_CONFLICT, WRONG_STATE, and INTERNAL_ERROR.
contractFindings.action: Keep precise Rust domain and store errors internal, then map them once at the Control Plane HTTP seam without leaking storage facts.
